results.title: direct to PostgREST: SQL sees the client-supplied x-forwarded-for
results.detail: POST http://localhost:3001/rpc/sec20_xff with x-forwarded-for=198.51.100.7 -> 200; SQL saw 1 address(es), client value present: true. A filter fed this way is client-controlled.

results.title: through the overwriting edge: SQL sees the edge's peer address, spoof gone
results.detail: POST http://localhost:8081/rpc/sec20_xff with the same client header -> 200; SQL saw 1 address(es), client value present: false; the single value is a private (RFC 1918) address, i.e. the edge's view of its peer: true.

results.title: the S04 filter: 403 on the direct spoof, 200 through the edge
results.detail: GET sec_own20 with x-forwarded-for=203.0.113.9: direct -> 403 PT403; via edge -> 200. The filter is only an allowlist when PostgREST is reachable from nowhere but the edge - a deployment property, not the function's.

results.title: cleanup
results.detail: table + RPC dropped; sec_ip_filter kept (the container references it for its life)
